title: RAG Application Load Balancing and Database Overload
alertSignatures: My RAG application is facing severe load issues because its receiving too many requests simultaneously. I dont want to limit the users responses and also dont want the database bottlenecks. I want every user request must be served without overloading the database
rootCause: High concurrent request volume causing database connection saturation and potential query bottlenecks.

successfulMitigations.action: Implement a request queue to decouple incoming requests from database processing
successfulMitigations.notes: Introduce a message queue (e.g., RabbitMQ or Kafka) to buffer incoming requests, allowing the database to process queries at a sustainable rate. [Confirmed: Verified effective by user via chatbot.]

successfulMitigations.action: Enable query caching for frequently accessed data
successfulMitigations.command: kubectl exec -it db-pod -- psql -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET shared_buffers = '2GB';"
successfulMitigations.notes: Increase shared buffers to improve cache hit rates and reduce the load on the database for repeated queries. [Confirmed: Verified effective by user via chatbot.]

successfulMitigations.action: Implement semantic caching for LLM responses
successfulMitigations.notes: Introduce a vector-based cache (e.g., using Redis with vector support or a dedicated semantic cache service) to store and retrieve similar LLM responses. This reduces the need to re-process identical or near-identical queries, significantly lowering database and LLM API load. [Confirmed: Verified effective by user via chatbot.]
successfulMitigations.sourceIncidentTitle: RAG Application Load Balancing and Database Overload

successfulMitigations.action: Optimize vector database indexing for faster search
successfulMitigations.command: kubectl exec -it vector-db-pod -- psql -c "CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_vector ON documents USING ivfflat (embedding);"
successfulMitigations.notes: Ensure the vector database (e.g., PostgreSQL with pgvector) has an appropriate index (like IVFFlat or HNSW) on the embedding column. This drastically reduces query latency for vector similarity searches, which are often the bottleneck in RAG applications. [Confirmed: Verified effective by user via chatbot.]
successfulMitigations.sourceIncidentTitle: RAG Application Load Balancing and Database Overload

successfulMitigations.action: Decouple LLM calls with async workers
successfulMitigations.notes: Move LLM API calls to a separate async worker pool. This prevents the main application threads from blocking on slow LLM responses, allowing the application to handle more concurrent requests and improve overall throughput. [Confirmed: Verified effective by user via chatbot.]
successfulMitigations.sourceIncidentTitle: RAG Application Load Balancing and Database Overload

successfulMitigations.action: Implement PgBouncer for efficient database connection pooling
successfulMitigations.notes: Instead of increasing max_connections (which failed previously), use PgBouncer to multiplex connections. This allows the application to maintain a large pool of client connections while the database only maintains a smaller, sustainable pool of server connections, drastically reducing connection overhead and context switching.
successfulMitigations.sourceIncidentTitle: RAG Application Load Balancing and Database Overload

successfulMitigations.action: Offload read-heavy vector searches to read replicas
successfulMitigations.notes: Configure the application to route read-only vector similarity searches and document retrievals to PostgreSQL read replicas. This distributes the read load away from the primary database, ensuring that write operations and critical transactions are not blocked by high-volume read queries.
successfulMitigations.sourceIncidentTitle: RAG Application Load Balancing and Database Overload

successfulMitigations.action: Implement LLM response streaming with backpressure
successfulMitigations.notes: Enable streaming for LLM responses to reduce perceived latency and allow the application to release resources earlier in the request lifecycle. Combine this with backpressure mechanisms to prevent the async worker pool from being overwhelmed by slow LLM responses, ensuring stable throughput.
successfulMitigations.sourceIncidentTitle: RAG Application Load Balancing and Database Overload

failedMitigations.command: kubectl exec -it db-pod -- psql -c "ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = 200;"
failedMitigations.failureOutcome: Simply increasing the connection pool didn't reduce the load on the server although it improved the rate limiting
